title: STEAM HARDWARE TOPOLOGY — Three Objects, Two Tethers

steam_deck.name: Steam Deck v1 (deckGate)
steam_deck.connection: USB-C tether to Steam Dock (single cable = life support)
steam_deck.note: The Deck IS ephemeral. It blinks in and out of existence based on a single cable.

steam_dock.name: Steam Dock (V2 Link)
steam_dock.nature: PERSISTENT — has its own power, keeps Deck alive
steam_dock.role: Life support for Deck + network bridge + USB hub
steam_dock.connection_to_deck: USB-C (the tether that gives the Deck life)
steam_dock.rj45_plan: Plug into Flint (GL-Net router) → direct LAN backbone

steam_link_v1.name: Steam Link Gen 1
steam_link_v1.nature: PERSISTENT — own power supply, independent node
steam_link_v1.role: PNS test node — peripherals + HDMI relay
steam_link_v1.rj45_plan: Plug into MikroTik → direct LAN backbone
steam_link_v1.usb_plan: Attach peripherals — controllers, sensors, USB devices
steam_link_v1.hdmi_plan: Output to Vizio TV (or other display)

tether.meaning: This cable IS the Deck's existence. Remove it = death.

dock_to_lan.gives: Deck gets wired LAN through the dock

link_to_lan.gives: Steam Link becomes a wired LAN node with USB + HDMI

topology_ascii: USB-C │ HDMI USB-A            USB×2 │ HDMI  │ power

two_new_rj45s.effect: Both Steam devices become WIRED LAN citizens, no WiFi needed
